The paraneoplastic hypothesis: an immune response raised against the tumour also recognises the nervous system. The group that found ZSCAN1 autoantibodies confirmed the protein in tumour and in healthy brain tissue and read tumour-associated ROHHAD as a paediatric paraneoplastic neurological syndrome. A Japanese survey found higher antibody titres in patients with a tumour, and in one patient the titre tended to fall after tumour resection or immunosuppressive therapy. The antibodies have also been found in patients without a tumour, so a tumour is not required for them.

Proposed, not shown. What points from the immune findings to the hypothalamus is thin: antibodies that bind hypothalamus and pituitary in one child, focal hypothalamic inflammation on imaging in one adolescent, and improvement after immunotherapy in a few patients, against no benefit in others. No step between an antibody and the loss of hypothalamic function has been demonstrated.
The weight gain is attributed to hypothalamic dysfunction, through hyperphagia and reduced energy expenditure. The lesion within the hypothalamus is not identified.
Hyperphagia is named as one of the two routes from hypothalamic dysfunction to the weight gain.

Disordered water balance is the most frequent manifestation of the hypothalamic dysfunction in one series, and a review places the sodium abnormality with the hypothalamus and the circumventricular organs.

nodes.description: Autoantibodies to the zinc finger protein ZSCAN1 were validated in 7 of 9 children in a study of paraneoplastic ROHHAD and in none of 125 controls. A second group then found them in patients without a tumour: of 6 with paired serum and cerebrospinal fluid, 5 (4 children and 1 adult) had the antibodies in cerebrospinal fluid only and 1 in both, while 7 further patients with serum only and 199 controls were negative. A third group reported serum positivity in over 85 per cent of its patients. A Japanese nationwide survey, which tested for anti-ZSCAN1 and anti-Nax antibodies, found antibodies in 70 per cent of 30 cases; its abstract does not divide the figure between the two. Other signs of an immune process come from one or two patients each: intrathecal oligoclonal bands, antibodies against hypothalamus and pituitary, and inflammatory cerebrospinal fluid with focal inflammation of the hypothalamus and periaqueductal grey matter on imaging. None of this shows that the antibodies cause the disease (see the discussions).

nodes.description: Symptoms of autonomic dysregulation began at a median of 3.6 years in the series that named the syndrome, and a systematic review puts dysautonomia at a median of 4.95 years. A series of 10 children found it in all, with strabismus the commonest sign. Reported signs also include disordered temperature control, abnormal pupils, bradycardia that needed a pacemaker, a raised pain threshold and gut dysmotility. Its cause is as unknown as that of the hypothalamic dysfunction, and no edge joins the two nodes.

nodes.description: Tried on the hypothesis of an immune cause, with mixed results and no controlled trial. Two children improved in behaviour and neuropsychological function after high-dose cyclophosphamide, one of them after a transient response to rituximab. An adolescent improved after intravenous steroids, immunoglobulins and long-term mycophenolate. Against that, three children given intravenous immunoglobulin as compassionate therapy had no significant benefit, and a child treated with plasmapheresis, methylprednisolone, an anti-CD20 antibody and azathioprine improved only for a time and died. A 2024 review sums up the benefit of immunosuppressive agents as variable.

nodes.description: A neural crest tumour was reported in 56 per cent of the patients in a systematic review of 43 individual patient descriptions, and 70 per cent of those tumours were diagnosed within two years of the first weight gain; the other 44 per cent had no tumour reported. Ganglioneuroma is the commonest type, and ganglioneuroblastoma also occurs. An earlier series of 13 patients put the proportion as high as 40 per cent and described the tumours as usually differentiated and without a significant effect on prognosis. Whether the tumour starts the syndrome or only accompanies it is not settled. One hypothesis holds that, where there is a tumour, it sets off an immune response against the nervous system (see the edge to Anti-Neural Autoimmunity).

evidence.reference_title: Delineation of late onset hypoventilation associated with hypothalamic dysfunction syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Tumor predisposition is more frequent than initially suspected and as high as 40% in this series. These tumors of the sympathetic nervous system (TSNS) are usually differentiated and do not significantly worsen the prognosis.

nodes.description: Puberty may be early. Precocious puberty is listed among the manifestations of hypothalamic dysfunction in a series of 10 children, and it is one of the two endocrinopathies that the European guideline on congenital central hypoventilation syndrome names when it describes ROHHAD. A systematic review found central precocious puberty in 7 of 48 patients reported individually (15 per cent). The opposite disturbance, hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, has its own row.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical Description of Ten Pediatric Patients with Clinical Signs of ROHHAD-NET Syndrome and Review of the Literature.
evidence.snippet: All patients had hypothalamic dysfunction, MAO 6.6 ± 1.3 years. Disorders of water balance were the most frequent manifestation (n = 10), followed by hyperprolactinemia, central hypothyroidism, growth hormone deficiency, adrenal insufficiency, precocious puberty, and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.

evidence.reference_title: Guidelines for diagnosis and management of congenital central hypoventilation syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Affected subjects typically present with rapid onset of obesity during early childhood; other key features develop later and include hypoventilation, endocrinopathies (water imbalance, precocious puberty), autonomic dysregulation (strabismus and disorders of temperature control) and sudden cardio-respiratory arrest.

nodes.description: Rapid weight gain in a previously healthy young child is usually the first sign. In the series that named the syndrome it began within the first 10 years of life, at a median of 3 years, and a later series of 10 children found it in all, as the first sign. It is not invariable: a Japanese survey recorded obesity in 72.7 per cent of cases at onset or at the first hospital visit, a French study describes four patients without rapid-onset obesity, and a systematic review counted rapid obesity in 40 of 48 patients reported individually (83 per cent) and in 71 of 110 patients reported in case series (65 per cent).

evidence.reference_title: Rapid-onset obesity with hypothalamic dysfunction, hypoventilation, and autonomic dysregulation presenting in childhood.
evidence.snippet: The most characteristic manifestations were the presentation of rapid-onset obesity in the first 10 years of life (median age at onset: 3 years), followed by hypothalamic dysfunction and then onset of symptoms of autonomic dysregulation (median age at onset: 3.6 years) with later onset of alveolar hypoventilation (median age at onset: 6.2 years).

evidence.snippet: Rapid-onset obesity, observed in all 10 patients, was the first clinical sign with a mean age at onset (MAO) of 5.1 ± 1.8 years.

nodes.description: One case, off label. A boy of 12 treated with setmelanotide, a melanocortin-4 receptor agonist, lost 28 per cent of his weight, with regression of hepatic steatosis, less ventilatory support and better behaviour. When the drug was stopped after 18 months he regained 10 per cent within three months. The authors take the response to suggest that the obesity may arise in the melanocortin-4 receptor pathway. It is a single uncontrolled observation.

evidence.reference_title: Melanocortin-4 Receptor Agonist Treatment of Hypothalamic Obesity in ROHHAD Syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Setmelanotide induced meaningful improvements, including substantial weight loss (28%, from 97 to 70 kg), measurable regression of hepatic steatosis as quantified by ultrasonography-based attenuation imaging, reduced ventilatory support, and a marked improvement in behavioral disorders that permitted the tapering of antipsychotic medication.

evidence.reference_title: Melanocortin-4 Receptor Agonist Treatment of Hypothalamic Obesity in ROHHAD Syndrome.
evidence.snippet: After 18 months of therapy, insurance coverage for the off-label use was refused, and treatment was discontinued, which resulted in significant weight gain within 3 months (10%, from 70 to 77 kg).

evidence.reference_title: Perioperative anesthetic management of children with congenital central hypoventilation syndrome and rapid-onset obesity with hypothalamic dysfunction, hypoventilation, and autonomic dysregulation undergoing thoracoscopic phrenic nerve-diaphragm pacemaker implantation.
evidence.snippet: Congenital Central Hypoventilation Syndrome and Rapid-Onset Obesity with Hypothalamic dysfunction, Hypoventilation, and Autonomic Dysregulation are rare neurocristopathies characterized by autonomic dysregulation including bradyarrhythmias, abnormal temperature control, and most significantly, abnormal control of breathing leading to tracheostomy and ventilator dependence as life support.

evidence.reference_title: Monozygotic twins discordant for ROHHAD phenotype.
evidence.snippet: From 8 to 12 years of age, the affected twin developed features characteristic of ROHHAD including obesity, alveolar hypoventilation, scoliosis, hypothalamic dysfunction (central diabetes insipidus, hypothyroidism, premature pubarche, and growth hormone deficiency), right paraspinal/thoracic ganglioneuroblastoma, seizures, and autonomic dysregulation including altered pain perception, large and sluggishly reactive pupils, hypothermia, and profound bradycardia that required a cardiac pacemaker.
